_readme: The narrator's script — one voice, two outputs. Each line's `text` IS the on-screen caption AND the words spoken aloud; they can never differ because they are one field. Audio files live at narrator/audio/<id>-<hash8>.mp3 where hash8 is djb2 of the text — edit a line here and its old audio silently stops matching (caption-only until `run-local.py --narrate` regenerates). Register: 7th-8th grade, one sentence at a time, warm and plain, zero system-speak — no 'analysis', 'generating', 'processing'. The narrator is a doorman, not a friend: it introduces, asks, fills waits, and hands off. It never chats.

lines.text: Talk or type. Messy is perfect.
Let me read what you wrote. This takes about half a minute.
Here's what I heard — six patterns, in your own words. Pick the three that feel most true.
You picked three patterns. Here's how I read each area of your life from what you wrote — fix any I got wrong.
Time, money, who's counting on you. Everything gets sized to this.
A few follow-ups. Skip any — silence is an answer too.
This is the part where I think. Give me a few minutes — I'm reading everything you told me.
Still here, still thinking. The big reads take a while.
Now I'll lay out the road for each goal. About a minute.
The road for each goal. This quarter is set; the rest comes into focus at the check-ins.
Last part — the small weekly things that get each step done.
Here's the week I drafted. Save it and it becomes your list.
